rule: rust-ipc-protocol: "Own the daemon's process lifecycle explicitly" / checklist 27 "disconnect and reconnect paths exercised" — one endpoint per host is the invariant every ptr_eq check in mirror.rs and router/mod.rs relies on
summary: `Machines::endpoint` is a check-then-act across two separate lock acquisitions, so concurrent callers each build and `connect()` a distinct `RemoteLink` for the same host; the loser is overwritten in the map but its actor and SSH child are never closed.
failure_scenario: Cold daemon, host `dev-box` configured. The periodic mirror reconcile and a user request that routes to `dev-box` call `Machines::endpoint("dev-box")` at the same time. Both see an empty `endpoints` map, both construct a `RemoteLink`, both spawn `connect()`. Two `ssh … fleetd connect` children are started, both perform Hello/Subscribe/GetSnapshot, and both stream every remote event. Only the second Arc survives in the map, so `close()` is never called on the first: its `run_link` actor reconnects forever and its `ChildStream` (and the SSH master it pins via ControlPersist) leaks for the lifetime of the daemon. Every config `rebuild` that adds a host repeats it. Additionally `Mirror::reconcile` (`Arc::ptr_eq(&observer.endpoint, &endpoint)`) and `start_event_pumps` (`Arc::ptr_eq(&pump.endpoint, endpoint)`) now see a different Arc than the one they registered, so they cancel and respawn observers/pumps and mark the fragment stale for no reason.
proposed_fix: Do the whole check-and-insert under one write guard: take `write(&self.endpoints)`, `match guard.entry(host.clone())` — return the occupied Arc, and only on `Vacant` construct the link, insert, and (after dropping the guard) spawn `connect()`. `Machines::install_endpoint` should go through the same guard so a test double cannot be clobbered by a racing lazy creation.
test_plan: Add `#[tokio::test(flavor = "multi_thread", worker_threads = 4)] async fn concurrent_endpoint_lookups_create_one_link()` in `crates/fleet-daemon/src/machines/registry.rs` tests: build `Machines` with a single `FakeMachine` provider (crates/fleet-daemon/src/testing/machines.rs), spawn 16 tasks that all `barrier.wait().await` then call `machines.endpoint(&host)`, join them, and assert (a) every returned Arc is `Arc::ptr_eq` to the first and (b) `FakeMachine` recorded exactly one `open_stream` call. Today two or more links are built and two streams are opened.
verify_reason: crates/fleet-daemon/src/machines/registry.rs:106-129: the read guard from `read(&self.endpoints).get(host)` is dropped before `self.get(host)` and nothing re-checks the map under `write(&self.endpoints).insert(...)` — a plain check-then-act. The function is fully synchronous (no await), so the interleaving needs two threads, and it has them: crates/fleet-daemon/src/main.rs:39 is a bare `#[tokio::main]` (multi-thread), and `Machines::endpoint` is called from unrelated tasks — Router::forward (services/router/mod.rs:135 via `fn endpoint` at :253), Router::route (:122), Router::start_event_pumps (:235) and Mirror::reconcile (services/mirror.rs:63-68), the last on a periodic task. The loser's `RemoteLink::connect()` is spawned (registry.rs:124) and its Arc is dropped from the map without `close()`, so its actor keeps reconnecting and its stream/ssh child leak; `rebuild` (registry.rs:74-89) only closes endpoints still in the map. The Arc::ptr_eq churn in mirror.rs:92 and router/mod.rs:242 is also real. Narrow window, but a real leak.
blast_radius: crates/fleet-daemon/src/machines/registry.rs only (plus a new test there and possibly crates/fleet-daemon/src/testing/machines.rs if the fake needs an open_stream counter). No caller signature changes; mirror.rs/router/mod.rs ptr_eq logic becomes correct without edits.
corrected_fix: Resolve the provider *before* taking the endpoints write guard (avoid nesting endpoints-write inside providers-read), then `match write(&self.endpoints).entry(host.clone())`: on Occupied return the existing Arc, on Vacant insert and remember that this call created it; drop the guard, and spawn `connect()` only for the newly created link. Do not route `install_endpoint` through the same guard as the proposal suggests — overwriting is what the test hook is for; the entry-based lazy path already stops clobbering it, since a pre-installed endpoint makes the entry Occupied.

rule: rust-ipc-protocol rule 3: "Put a deadline on every await that touches the wire — or a comment saying why not"; checklist 13
summary: `connected_loop` awaits `transport.send(encoded)` with no deadline and outside any `select!`, so a full SSH pipe wedges the link actor permanently — `RemoteLink::close()` awaits that task and never returns.
failure_scenario: The remote daemon applies its designed backpressure: `Connection::run` stops polling `reader.next()` once `pending.len() >= MAX_PENDING_REQUESTS` (crates/fleet-daemon/src/server/connection.rs:153). Fan out 64+ concurrent slow requests (e.g. a bulk worktree create) to one host and the remote stops reading; the SSH pipe and channel window fill; the local `transport.send` for request 65 returns `Pending` forever. From that moment the link actor is frozen: no shutdown observation, no reads, no `fail_pending`, so every caller blocked in `RemoteEndpoint::request` waits forever too (its `select!` only races `states.changed()`, and the state stays `Ready`). A config change then calls `Machines::rebuild` → `endpoint.close()`, which hangs on `task.await`, leaking the task, its `ChildStream` and its ssh child; daemon shutdown likewise never joins it.
proposed_fix: Bound and cancel the write the way the client does: add `const WRITE_BUDGET: Duration` next to `LinkOptions`, and replace the bare await with `tokio::select! { result = transport.send(encoded) => …, () = sleep(WRITE_BUDGET) => return "remote stream write timed out".to_owned(), changed = shutdown.changed() => return "remote link is closed".to_owned() }` so a stalled peer becomes a normal disconnect (pending failed, state `Down`, backoff reconnect) instead of a wedge.
test_plan: Add `#[tokio::test(start_paused = true)] async fn a_stalled_remote_write_does_not_wedge_close()` in `crates/fleet-daemon/src/machines/link.rs` tests: a provider whose `open_stream` returns one half of a `tokio::io::duplex(1024)` while the test holds the other half and never reads it after the handshake; drive the handshake, then issue requests with large `TerminalInput` payloads until the duplex buffer is full, then assert `tokio::time::timeout(Duration::from_secs(5), link.close()).await.is_ok()`. Today the timeout fires.
verify_reason: crates/fleet-daemon/src/machines/link.rs:459-480: inside the `commands.recv()` branch of `connected_loop`'s select, `transport.send(encoded).await` is a bare await; once that branch body runs, neither `shutdown.changed()` (:455) nor `transport.next()` (:482) is polled, so a peer that stops reading freezes the actor with no state transition (state stays Ready, `fail_pending` never runs). `RemoteLink::close` (link.rs:324-331) then blocks on `task.await` with no timeout and no abort fallback. The remote peer really does stop reading under load: crates/fleet-daemon/src/server/connection.rs:152 gates `reader.next()` on `pending.len() < MAX_PENDING_REQUESTS` (64). The contrast with the client is accurate — crates/fleet-client/src/connection.rs:412-451 races the write against `reader.next()` and a `WRITE_BUDGET` deadline. Callers of `RemoteLink::request` (link.rs:280-304) only race `states.changed()`, so they hang too.
blast_radius: crates/fleet-daemon/src/machines/link.rs (connected_loop, LinkOptions, close), crates/fleet-daemon/tests/remote_link.rs and the inline `mod tests` in link.rs (a write-budget constant is new tunable state), docs/REMOTE-MACHINES.md §5 (the deadline/backoff paragraph should name the new budget). No proto or client change.
corrected_fix: Do bound the write, but keep it cancel-correct: race `transport.send(encoded)` against a `sleep(options.write_budget)` **and** `shutdown.changed()`, returning a disconnect reason on either, so the existing `fail_pending` + `set_shared_down` + backoff path runs (the partially-encoded frame is irrelevant because the transport is dropped and re-established). Do not race it against `transport.next()` the way the client does — incoming frames here are events as well as responses and handling them mid-write would reorder `pending` bookkeeping. Add the budget to `LinkOptions` rather than a private const so tests can shrink it. Independently give `close()` a backstop: `tokio::time::timeout(..., task).await` then `task.abort()`, so a future wedge cannot leak a task even if the deadline is mistuned.

rule: CLAUDE.md non-negotiable: "docs/ is authoritative, not descriptive… When code and a doc disagree, one of them is a bug"; rust-ipc-protocol checklist 24
summary: The authoritative `RemoteEndpoint` trait listing in docs/REMOTE-MACHINES.md § 5 omits `nudge_reconnect`, a trait method the bootstrap flow depends on, and § 5's backoff paragraph never mentions the nudge or the retained permit.
failure_scenario: An implementor writing a new `MachineProvider`/endpoint (or a reviewer checking § 9 bootstrap against the code) reads § 5 as the complete contract, does not implement `nudge_reconnect`, and silently inherits the empty default — remote bootstrap then waits out the full 60 s backoff after the remote restart and `probe_for_build`'s 45 s `PROBE_TIMEOUT` fails with "did not report build … after restart" even though the remote daemon came up correctly.
proposed_fix: Add `fn nudge_reconnect(&self);` to the § 5 trait block and one sentence to the backoff paragraph: a nudge wakes a sleeping link, resets the backoff to its floor, and its permit is retained so a nudge racing a disconnect still shortens the following attempt (link.rs:307-314). Note the bootstrap caller in § 9.
test_plan: Add `crates/fleet-daemon/tests/docs_contract.rs::remote_endpoint_doc_block_lists_every_trait_method`: parse the `RemoteEndpoint` trait's method names out of `crates/fleet-daemon/src/machines/link.rs` (lines between `pub trait RemoteEndpoint` and its closing brace) and assert each name appears inside the first fenced `rust` block after `## 5. RemoteEndpoint and RemoteLink` in `docs/REMOTE-MACHINES.md`. It fails today on `nudge_reconnect`.
verify_reason: docs/REMOTE-MACHINES.md:95-104 lists the trait with eight methods and no `nudge_reconnect`; the real trait at crates/fleet-daemon/src/machines/link.rs:79-86 has it (with an empty default body), and crates/fleet-daemon/src/services/bootstrap.rs:279 calls it between the remote restart and `probe_for_build(..., PROBE_TIMEOUT)` (bootstrap.rs:20 = 45 s) precisely so the probe does not wait out a backoff that reaches 60 s (link.rs:61-62). `grep -rn -i nudge docs/` returns nothing, so §5's backoff paragraph and §9 are both silent. Doc-drift against a non-negotiable in CLAUDE.md.
blast_radius: docs/REMOTE-MACHINES.md §5 (and one sentence in §9). No code change; the optional contract test would add crates/fleet-daemon/tests/docs_contract.rs.
corrected_fix: Add the method to the doc block as `fn nudge_reconnect(&self) {}` — with the empty default, since that is the actual signature and implementors may omit it (the same way `last_snapshot_seen` is defaulted) — and describe the real semantics in the backoff paragraph: a nudge wakes a sleeping link, resets backoff to `backoff_min`, and its `Notify` permit is retained when the link is not sleeping so a nudge racing a disconnect shortens the following attempt. Skip the proposed parse-the-source contract test; it is brittle against rustfmt/doc rewrapping — a one-line note in the §5 review checklist is enough.

rule: rust-ipc-protocol checklist 27 / audit criterion 5: "a test that cannot fail"
summary: `nudge_on_a_connected_link_does_not_disturb_it` never connects the link, so it asserts nothing about the connected case; meanwhile the trait's own doc comment claims a nudge is a no-op on a connected link, which `RemoteLink::nudge_reconnect` deliberately is not.
failure_scenario: Someone "fixes" `nudge_reconnect` to honour its own doc comment by early-returning when `*self.state_tx.borrow() == LinkState::Ready`. Both existing nudge tests still pass (the connected one because it never connects, the sleeping one because it nudges a `Down` link), yet remote bootstrap regresses: `bootstrap.rs:279` nudges while the link is still `Ready` (the remote `kill -TERM` has not yet been noticed locally), the permit is now dropped, and the post-restart probe waits out the grown backoff and times out at `PROBE_TIMEOUT`.
proposed_fix: Correct the trait doc at link.rs:79-82 to state the actual contract — a nudge on a connected link is not observable immediately but retains a permit that shortens the next reconnect — and rewrite the test to actually connect: use `FakeMachine` (crates/fleet-daemon/src/testing/machines.rs:34) so `connect()` reaches `LinkState::Ready`, assert a nudge opens no new stream while Ready, then force a disconnect and assert the very next attempt happens at `backoff_min` because the permit was retained.
test_plan: Replace the test with `#[tokio::test(start_paused = true)] async fn a_nudge_while_ready_is_retained_for_the_next_disconnect()`: connect a `RemoteLink` over `FakeMachine`, assert `state() == LinkState::Ready` and that `nudge_reconnect()` triggers no additional `open_stream`; drop the fake's peer half to force a disconnect and assert the next `open_stream` is observed immediately rather than after `backoff_min`. Adding the early-return `Ready` guard to `nudge_reconnect` must make this test fail — the current test passes either way.
verify_reason: crates/fleet-daemon/src/machines/link.rs:959-970: the test named `nudge_on_a_connected_link_does_not_disturb_it` never calls `connect()`, so `started` is false, no actor exists, and `provider.attempts() == 0` / `state() == Down` hold for any implementation — it asserts nothing about the connected case its name claims. The doc/impl mismatch it points at is also real: the trait doc (link.rs:82) says 'Implementations must treat this as a no-op for a link that is already connected', while `RemoteLink::nudge_reconnect` (link.rs:306-314) stores a permit unconditionally via `notify_one()`, consumed at the next disconnect (link.rs:383) to reset backoff — deliberate, per its own comment, and depended on by bootstrap.rs:277-279, whose comment ('a Ready link is unaffected') repeats the same inaccurate framing. The regression the finding describes — an early-return-when-Ready 'fix' passing both existing tests while breaking post-restart bootstrap — follows directly.
blast_radius: crates/fleet-daemon/src/machines/link.rs (trait doc at :79-86, the inline test at :959) and the comment at crates/fleet-daemon/src/services/bootstrap.rs:277-278; may need an open_stream/attempt counter on the fake in crates/fleet-daemon/src/testing/machines.rs. Docs change rides with ipc-nudge-doc-drift.
corrected_fix: As proposed, with one adjustment: assert the retained permit by advancing a paused clock rather than by 'observed immediately'. Use `#[tokio::test(start_paused = true)]`, connect over the fake to Ready, nudge, assert no extra `open_stream`, force a disconnect, then assert the next attempt happens at `backoff_min` after `tokio::time::advance(backoff_min)` and not before — wall-clock 'immediately' assertions in this file are what made the sibling test at link.rs:930-955 rely on real `sleep(50ms)`/`sleep(3s)`, which is flaky under load. Fix the trait doc in the same commit so the corrected contract, not the test, is the source of truth.

rule: rust-gpui-testing checklist, Shape and hygiene: "Is the test named as a sentence stating the invariant?" — the name is the contract
summary: `nudge_on_a_connected_link_does_not_disturb_it` never connects the link; its own comment says "Not connected yet", so the invariant in its name — a nudge on an established link must not tear it down — is untested while the name advertises that it is covered.
failure_scenario: Change `nudge_reconnect` to unconditionally drop the current transport and restart the connect loop (the obvious "make the nudge always work" refactor). Every existing test still passes — this one is `Down` and asserts `attempts() == 0`, and `nudge_wakes_a_sleeping_link_and_restarts_backoff_from_the_floor` (`:922`) *wants* a new attempt. In production every `nudge_reconnect` on a healthy SSH link now kills the session's remote terminals and re-runs the handshake.

It fails the moment `nudge_reconnect` stops checking the current state.

blast_radius: crates/fleet-daemon/src/machines/link.rs `mod tests` (rename plus a new connectable provider), or crates/fleet-daemon/tests/remote_link.rs if the new test goes there — that file's provider at :327-349 gains an attempt counter, affecting its other tests' fixture construction. corrected_fix: Rename to `nudge_on_a_link_that_never_connected_is_inert` (the body is a legitimate test of exactly that). For the real one, note the proposal's fixture claim is wrong: crates/fleet-daemon/tests/remote_link.rs:327-349 wraps an inner `machine.open_stream()` and exposes no `attempts()` counter, and the misnamed test lives in an in-src private `mod tests` that cannot reach `tests/`. So either add a counting loopback provider inside link.rs's `mod tests` (an `open_stream` returning a `tokio::io::duplex` half backed by a scripted Hello responder, incrementing the same `attempts` counter), or put the new test in tests/remote_link.rs and extend that fixture with an attempt counter. rule: rust-workspace-architecture: "`expect` only for a genuine static invariant with a message" / checklist §Errors — "Is there a new `.unwrap()` in production code? … The 22 surviving `expect()` calls are static invariants"
summary: `fleetd` startup `expect()`s that the contents of the on-disk `$FLEET_HOME/daemon-id` file parse as a `HostId`, so any file the daemon did not write itself turns daemon startup into a panic instead of a handled error.
failure_scenario: `$FLEET_HOME/daemon-id` contains `local`, `MyLaptop`, `host.example.com`, or two lines (`abc\ndef`) — from a hand edit, a restored backup, a synced home directory, or a torn write. `HostId::try_from` returns `Err`, `expect` panics inside `Services::build`, and `fleetd` aborts on every start with a backtrace instead of reporting a bad identity file; the user has no error message pointing at the file and no way to recover except deleting a file they cannot know about.
proposed_fix: Make `load_or_create_daemon_id` return a validated `HostId`: on a read whose contents fail `HostId::try_from`, `tracing::warn!` naming the path and the reason, then generate and persist a fresh UUID (the same path already taken for an empty/unreadable file). Keep `expect` only for the freshly generated UUID, which really is a static invariant.
test_plan: Add to `crates/fleet-daemon/src/services/composition.rs`'s existing test module, beside `daemon_id_is_stable_for_one_fleet_home` (composition.rs:260): write `local\n` into `home.join("daemon-id")` before calling `build()`, then assert `Services::build` returns and `first.daemon_id()` is a valid `HostId` different from `"local"`. Today that test panics with `persisted daemon identity must be a valid host id`.
verify_reason: crates/fleet-daemon/src/services/composition.rs:152-154 is exactly as quoted: `HostId::try_from(daemon_id.as_str()).expect("persisted daemon identity must be a valid host id")`, inside `pub(super) fn build(...) -> Self` (composition.rs:45-52), which returns no Result, so the failure is a panic on the daemon's startup path. The input is unvalidated file content: services/mod.rs:151-158 returns any non-empty trimmed line from `$FLEET_HOME/daemon-id`. crates/fleet-core/src/ids.rs:155-168 rejects the literal `local` and anything outside /^[a-z0-9-]+$/, so `MyLaptop`, `host.example.com`, `local`, or a torn two-line file all panic. The self-written value (uuid v4 hyphenated lowercase) is always valid, so this only bites on an externally modified/restored file — narrow, but the contents of a file is not the 'static invariant' the guide reserves expect for.
blast_radius: crates/fleet-daemon/src/services/composition.rs (build signature or its caller), crates/fleet-daemon/src/services/mod.rs:151-164, crates/fleet-daemon/src/main.rs if the error is threaded to the binary, and the existing test `daemon_id_is_stable_for_one_fleet_home` (composition.rs:260-287) plus any test constructing Services::new.
corrected_fix: Prefer failing loudly over silently rotating the identity: `load_or_create_daemon_id` should return `DaemonResult<HostId>` (or the caller should surface an anyhow error from main.rs) with a message naming `$FLEET_HOME/daemon-id` and the validation reason, because the daemon_id is the host identity remote peers key on (machines/link.rs:567, docs/REMOTE-MACHINES.md:42-43) — silently minting a fresh UUID, as the proposal suggests, breaks every existing remote link without telling anyone. If a self-healing path is wanted anyway, rename the bad file to `daemon-id.invalid` and `tracing::warn!` both the old and the new id so the change is traceable. Note that `build` is infallible today, so either the error must be threaded through `Services::new`/`build` or the validation must move up into main.rs before construction.

rule: rust-workspace-architecture: "Never `let _ =` a fallible call … a silently swallowed error is the bug you cannot find later"
summary: The daemon's persistent identity is written with `let _ = std::fs::write(...)`, so a failed write silently yields a brand-new identity on every restart while the doc comment promises a stable one.
failure_scenario: `$FLEET_HOME` is on a full or read-only volume, or `daemon-id` exists with mode 0 after a bad restore. `std::fs::write` fails, the error is discarded, and every `fleetd` start hands out a different UUID. Remote peers see a new `daemon_id`/`host_id` on each restart of the same machine, so link-identity and self-link detection reason about a machine whose identity keeps changing — with nothing in the log to say the identity file was never written.
proposed_fix: Handle the write: `if let Err(error) = std::fs::write(&path, format!("{id}\n")) { tracing::warn!(path = %path.display(), %error, "could not persist the daemon identity; it will change on the next restart"); }` — and do the same for the discarded `create_dir_all` result on the line above.
test_plan: In `crates/fleet-daemon/src/services/composition.rs`'s test module, build `Services` twice against a home directory made read-only (`std::fs::set_permissions` 0o555) and assert with `tracing_test`/a capturing subscriber that a warning naming `daemon-id` was emitted. Before the fix no log line exists and the two `daemon_id()` values differ with no diagnostic.
verify_reason: crates/fleet-daemon/src/services/mod.rs:159-164 is verbatim as quoted — `if std::fs::create_dir_all(home).is_ok() { let _ = std::fs::write(path, format!("{id}\n")); }` — with no comment, and it is not a channel send, so it violates the CLAUDE.md non-negotiable directly. The value really is the wire identity (machines/link.rs:560-570 sends it as `host_id` in Hello; docs/REMOTE-MACHINES.md:42-43 documents it as persisted), and the doc comment at services/mod.rs:144-146 promises stability. One correction to the finding's scenario: the 'full or read-only $FLEET_HOME' case is mostly unreachable, because main.rs:53-55 already does `std::fs::create_dir_all(layout.logs_dir())?` and opens the rotating log before Services are built, so an unwritable home aborts startup earlier with a real error. The reachable case is narrower — a `daemon-id` file that exists but is unreadable and unwritable (bad restore, wrong owner) — but the swallow is still real and undiagnosable.
blast_radius: crates/fleet-daemon/src/services/mod.rs only; the composition.rs test module if a log-capturing assertion is added (note the suggested chmod-0o555 test is unreliable when tests run as root in CI containers — assert on the injected failure path instead, or skip the test).
corrected_fix: Handle both results, not just the write: `match std::fs::create_dir_all(home) { Err(error) => tracing::warn!(...), Ok(()) => if let Err(error) = std::fs::write(&path, format!("{id}\n")) { tracing::warn!(path = %path.display(), %error, "could not persist the daemon identity; it will change on the next restart") } }`. Fold this into the same change as workspace-hygiene-daemon-id-expect-panics — both live in `load_or_create_daemon_id` and both are about the same file — rather than shipping two separate commits touching the same eight lines.

rule: rust-workspace-architecture: "Write log macros fully qualified, and make the filter runtime-configurable … `fleetd` installs none, so `RUST_LOG` is silently ignored by the daemon"
summary: `fleetd`'s subscriber is built with no `EnvFilter`, so it is hard-capped at INFO: `RUST_LOG` does nothing for the daemon and all 16 of its `tracing::debug!`/`trace!` sites can never emit — including the one whose comment says the redacted argv "stays in the debug log".
evidence:
crates/fleet-daemon/src/main.rs:57-59:
```rust
    tracing_subscriber::fmt()
        .with_writer((|| std::io::stderr()).and(file_writer))
        .init();
```
`SubscriberBuilder`'s default filter is `Subscriber::DEFAULT_MAX_LEVEL` = `LevelFilter::INFO` (tracing-subscriber-0.3.23/src/fmt/mod.rs:349, :470), and `crates/fleet-daemon/Cargo.toml` takes `tracing-subscriber.workspace = true` without the `env-filter` feature. The app does it correctly — crates/fleet-app/src/shell/root/bootstrap.rs:29-34 uses `EnvFilter::try_from_default_env()`. The cost is explicit at crates/fleet-daemon/src/adapters/shell.rs:171-176: `// The argv itself stays in the debug log.` followed by `tracing::debug!(command = %description, %error, "shell command failed");`.
failure_scenario: A shell/git command fails inside the daemon and the user is shown only the redacted `subcommand(&command)` text. They follow the code comment and run `RUST_LOG=fleet_daemon=debug fleet daemon restart` to see the full argv; the filter is ignored, the debug record is dropped by the max-level cap, and the argv is unobtainable at any log level — the diagnostic path the code deliberately provides does not exist at runtime.
proposed_fix: Add `env-filter` to `fleet-daemon`'s `tracing-subscriber` features and build the subscriber as the app does: `let filter = EnvFilter::try_from_default_env().unwrap_or_else(|_| EnvFilter::new("info")); tracing_subscriber::fmt().with_env_filter(filter).with_writer(...).init();`. Document the variable in the `## Logs` section of docs/DEVELOPMENT.md:145, which currently covers only `fleet`.
test_plan: Extend `crates/fleet-daemon/tests/server_process.rs` (which already launches the real `fleetd`): start the daemon with `RUST_LOG=fleet_daemon=debug`, drive one failing shell-backed request, then assert `$FLEET_HOME/logs/fleetd.log` contains a `DEBUG` line. It fails before the change because the file holds no record above INFO.
verify_reason: crates/fleet-daemon/src/main.rs:57-59 builds `tracing_subscriber::fmt().with_writer(...).init()` with no filter; crates/fleet-daemon/Cargo.toml:39 is `tracing-subscriber.workspace = true` and the workspace entry (Cargo.toml:75) is plain `"0.3"`, so `env-filter` is not enabled for this crate and no EnvFilter appears anywhere under crates/fleet-daemon/src (grep for EnvFilter/with_max_level returns nothing). SubscriberBuilder's default filter is LevelFilter::INFO, and `.init()` sets the global max level from it, so all 16 `tracing::debug!`/`trace!` sites in crates/fleet-daemon/src (counted) are dead at runtime — including the one at adapters/shell.rs:171-176 whose own comment says the argv 'stays in the debug log'. fleet-app does it correctly (shell/root/bootstrap.rs:28-35, with features = ["env-filter"] at crates/fleet-app/Cargo.toml:30), and docs/DEVELOPMENT.md:145-150 documents RUST_LOG only for `fleet`, confirming the daemon side was never wired.

corrected_fix: The proposed fix is right; two details. Add `tracing-subscriber = { workspace = true, features = ["env-filter"] }` to crates/fleet-daemon/Cargo.toml (do not rely on feature unification from fleet-app — a `cargo build -p fleet-daemon` would then fail). Keep the existing dual stderr+file writer and the `_log_guard` binding intact when rewriting the builder chain; dropping that guard silently loses buffered file output. Update docs/DEVELOPMENT.md §Logs in the same commit, per the docs-ride-with-code rule.

rule: rust-workspace-architecture: "`docs/` is authoritative, not descriptive … a change contradicting a doc is a bug in one of the two and both move in the same commit"; CLAUDE.md non-negotiables
summary: docs/DEVELOPMENT.md tells the reader that `make run` does not restart the daemon and that restarting is explicit, but the Makefile makes `run` depend on `restart`, so following the doc's PTY-preservation advice loses the sessions it promises to keep.
evidence:
docs/DEVELOPMENT.md:44-45:
```
`make run` does **not** restart the daemon: an already-running `fleetd` keeps its terminal
sessions across an app rebuild. Restarting is explicit, through `make restart` or:
```
Makefile:24-25 says the opposite, and its own help text agrees with the code, not the doc:
```make
run: restart ## Build, restart fleetd, and open Fleet (ARGS="..." supported)
	$(RUNTIME_ENV) "$(FLEET)" $(ARGS)
```
`restart: build` at Makefile:27-28 then runs `fleet daemon restart`. The same doc's own command table (docs/DEVELOPMENT.md:13) already describes `make run` as "build the workspace and open Fleet".
failure_scenario: A developer with long-running agent PTYs reads line 44, believes `make run` is the safe rebuild path, and runs it. `run` depends on `restart`, which issues `fleet daemon restart`; as the same doc states at line 52, "PTYs do not survive it" — every terminal session is killed, which is precisely the outcome the paragraph promised to avoid.
proposed_fix: Pick the intended behaviour and move both in one commit. Either rewrite docs/DEVELOPMENT.md:44-45 to say `make run` restarts `fleetd` (and point at `cargo run -p fleet-app` / running `$(FLEET)` directly as the session-preserving path), or drop the `restart` prerequisite from Makefile:24 so `run: build` and the documented contract holds.
test_plan: Add a case to `scripts/tests/` (already wired into `make test-scripts`) that runs `make -n run` in a scratch copy and asserts whether `fleet daemon restart` appears, matched against the documented claim; alternatively assert the prerequisite directly with `make --print-data-base`. Written against the doc's wording, it fails today because `make -n run` emits `fleet daemon restart`.
verify_reason: Makefile:24-25 is `run: restart` with the help text 'Build, restart fleetd, and open Fleet', and Makefile:27-28 is `restart: build` running `fleet daemon restart`. docs/DEVELOPMENT.md:44-45 says the opposite in bold: '`make run` does **not** restart the daemon: an already-running `fleetd` keeps its terminal sessions across an app rebuild.' The same doc states at line 52 that 'PTYs do not survive it', so the contradiction has a concrete user cost, and the doc's own command table at line 12 ('build the workspace and open Fleet') is silent about the restart, which is how the drift went unnoticed. Under the docs-are-authoritative rule this is a bug in one of the two by definition.
blast_radius: docs/DEVELOPMENT.md lines 12 and 44-52 only, if the doc is the side that moves. If the Makefile were changed instead: Makefile:24, `run-release`, and every contributor workflow plus CLAUDE.md's 'run `make restart` after changing daemon code' guidance.
corrected_fix: The Makefile is almost certainly the intended behaviour — `make daemon: restart` and the `run` help text both assume the restart, and running a freshly built app against a stale daemon is exactly what `make restart` exists to prevent. So fix the doc, not the Makefile: rewrite docs/DEVELOPMENT.md:44-45 to say `make run` restarts fleetd (and that PTYs do not survive it), and point at running `$(FLEET)` / `cargo run -p fleet-app` directly as the session-preserving path. Also amend the line-12 table entry so both places agree. Dropping the `restart` prerequisite instead would silently reintroduce app/daemon version skew for every developer and is the riskier direction. The proposed `make -n run` test is unnecessary churn for a two-line doc fix.
